M1-T3.title: Define the typed trace contract: Run, Agent, Message, ToolCall, Event
tests_added: src/types/trace.test.ts — 8 tests: the ingest constant is pinned to exactly 'agent_messages' and EVENT_KINDS is exactly ['run_start','run_end','message','tool_call']; a full Run + Agent/Message/ToolCall/Event fixture is attached with `satisfies` so any renamed/dropped required field breaks compilation; broadcast is modelled as to===null; a tool call may stand alone (messageId===null); the isMessageEvent/isToolCallEvent/isLifecycleEvent guards narrow correctly and only for their own kind; each narrowed arm carries its precise member shape (expectTypeOf); the union is exhaustively switchable on `kind` with no default arm; ordering fields (at/sequence/seed) are integers so the timeline is a total order
M1-T3.verification: npm run verify green end-to-end — lint 0w/0e (--deny-warnings); format:check clean; typecheck clean; test 18/18 passed (4 files, +8 new); build green (366ms)
M1-T3.notes: The trace contract every other module speaks is now typed in src/types/ (pure data, zero deps — no three.js, no DOM, no clock, so it is jsdom-safe and importable everywhere). Declared the five PRD-mandated entities: Agent (with a derived parentId fan-out link, precomputed send/receive counts, per-agent token/cost attribution), Message (from/to with to===null as broadcast, raw body kept alongside a decoded MessagePayload + mirrored action, status, epoch-ms `at`), ToolCall (agent-attributed, messageId nullable, args/duration/cost), and Event as a discriminated union on `kind` over run_start | run_end | message | tool_call, each arm carrying a precise payload plus the shared deterministic ordering pair (`at` epoch-ms + `sequence`). Run ties them together with a required `seed` (determinism is a product requirement per PRD §5, so the layout seed is part of the contract) and a precomputed RunMeta for the HUD. Design choices that matter downstream: (1) ids and `sequence` are DERIVED from the trace, never random — that is what lets M1-T5 pin byte-identical output and M2 render a stable shape; (2) all timestamps are numbers (epoch ms), never strings/Dates, so ordering is total and timezone-free; (3) NO layout coordinates live here — the contract carries facts only, layout is M2's derived output; (4) TraceSource is a one-member union pinned to 'agent_messages' with a note not to widen it before M6-T5 (single-format ingest rule). Deliberately did NOT build the parser (M1-T4) or the normalization/counting pass (M1-T5) — this task defines shapes only; the Agent/Run counts in the contract are fields the later passes will populate. Chose const-unions over TS enums because tsconfig sets erasableSyntaxOnly. NEXT: M1-T4 (agent_messages export adapter: Supabase rows -> trace contract).

M1-T4.title: `agent_messages` export adapter (Supabase rows → trace contract)

M1-T4.notes: The ONE v1 ingest path is now real. parseAgentMessagesExport (src/adapter/) turns a recorded Supabase agent_messages export — JSON text or an already-parsed row array, and it unwraps a {data}/{rows}/{agent_messages} REST-style body — into a normalized Run from src/types/ (M1-T3). Pure: no network, no clock, no DOM, no three.js, so it is jsdom-safe and importable anywhere. Mapping: each row → a Message (to_agent NULL ⇒ to === null broadcast; body kept verbatim and decoded into a MessagePayload when it is a JSON object; action mirrored for fast grouping; status coerced read/unread; created_at → epoch ms via Date.parse). When the decoded payload carries an action it ALSO yields a ToolCall (id tc_<rowId>, agent = sender, args = payload minus `action`, durationMs null, costUsd 0) — v1 rows have no spawn/tool columns, so the declared action is the only tool signal available; both surface as MessageEvent / ToolCallEvent, bracketed by one run_start ... run_end pair with a contiguous 0-based sequence. Agents are derived from the distinct from_agent/to_agent names (alphabetically ordered for a stable array) with messagesSent, messagesReceived (a broadcast counts per recipient — every agent except its sender), an involvement-based first/last-seen window (a message counts for BOTH sender and recipient), and 0 tokens/cost because v1 carries none — never invented. DETERMINISM IS THE POINT (PRD §5): rows are canonically ordered by created_at then row id BEFORE anything is derived and duplicate primary keys are rejected, so the same export parses byte-identically and a shuffled export yields the identical Run (both pinned by tests); the run id and layout seed are hashed (FNV-1a) from the normalized messages, so identical input ⇒ identical id/seed and a different input ⇒ a different, stable one. Deliberately NOT done here (kept out of scope so the adapter stays a mechanical row→contract map): role inference and the fan-out/handoff/parentage edge model, which are M2-T4 — every Agent.role is 'unknown' and every parentId is null at this stage — and the deeper normalization/hardening pass, which is M1-T5. Malformed input is rejected with a typed TraceParseError (bad JSON, a non-array value, a non-object row, a missing from_agent/id, an unparseable created_at, a duplicate id) rather than silently dropped, so a corrupt export fails loudly. M1-T5.title: TraceModel normalization pass with deterministic output + tests
tests_added: src/model/traceModel.test.ts — 22 tests. Canonical shape: a normalized adapter Run is reproduced byte-for-byte; normalization is a fixed point; Event.sequence is contiguous 0-based in canonical order; agents sort by id and messages/tool calls by (at, id); every derived field (per-agent counts, span, RunMeta) is recomputed, so a deliberately-corrupted input normalizes back to the truth; role/parentId are preserved for M2-T4; an empty run normalizes to itself; the input is not mutated. Determinism: byte-identical across calls; unchanged when every array is reversed AND every sequence zeroed; m_9 precedes m_10 (natural id order). compareModelIds: digit runs compared numerically, the rest lexically. Integrity: unknown sender, unknown recipient, tool call with an unknown agent, tool call referencing an unknown message, an agent-attributed lifecycle event, an absent/unknown message-event agent, a message event whose mirror disagrees with its message, duplicate ids in all four collections, and a non-finite timestamp all throw TraceModelError.
M1-T5.verification: npm run lint clean (0 warnings / 0 errors, 18 files); npm run typecheck clean; npm run test 66/66 passed (6 files, +22 new); npm run build green (347ms); prettier --check clean on the 3 new files
M1-T5.notes: The pure data layer now has its normalization seam. normalizeTrace (src/model/) turns ANY Run-shaped object into a TraceModel — a Run with every contract invariant enforced — and is the single place those promises are pinned (src/types/trace.ts states the normalizer owns Event.sequence). It does four things: (1) CANONICALIZES ORDER — agents by id, messages/toolCalls by (at, id), events by (at, kind-rank, id) via a natural comparator so m_9 sorts before m_10 (a plain lexical sort would not); (2) ASSIGNS Event.sequence as a contiguous 0-based index over that canonical order; (3) RECOMPUTES every derived/precomputed field from the facts — per-agent send/receive counts, the involvement-based active window, token/cost attribution (a broadcast counts per recipient), the startedAt/endedAt span and the whole RunMeta — so a stale count in the input cannot survive; (4) VALIDATES referential integrity (unique ids; every message/tool-call/event reference resolves; lifecycle events unattributed and message/tool-call events attributed; a message event agrees with its message) and throws a typed TraceModelError rather than silently repairing a broken run. DETERMINISM IS THE DELIVERABLE (PRD §5): the model is byte-identical across calls AND independent of the input's array order and its sequence values — pinned by a test that reverses every array and zeroes every sequence and still expects byte-equality — and normalizeTrace is a fixed point. Composition is pinned too: normalizing an adapter-produced Run reproduces it byte-for-byte, so the recomputation provably agrees with the adapter's derivation. Deliberately NOT done here: re-deriving Agent.role/parentId (the M2-T4 edge model owns them, so they are preserved as-is), the fixtures (M1-T6) and the timeline/playhead (M1-T7). No coordinates, no three.js, no clock — pure and jsdom-tested; nothing about the look is asserted (human-held M5-T5). NEXT: M1-T6 (deterministic trace fixtures: fan-out, loop, dead branch, handoff chain).

M1-T6.title: Deterministic trace fixtures: synthetic runs (fan-out, loop, dead branch, handoff chain)

M1-T7.title: Timeline/playhead model over the event stream + tests
tests_added: src/timeline/timeline.test.ts — 36 tests. buildTimeline: returns a Timeline sharing the model's canonical events, agentIds in model order, startedAt/endedAt/spanMs mirroring the model; collapses the stream into distinct ascending stops (first === startedAt, last === endedAt); folds several same-instant events onto one stop; byte-identical across calls; a valid empty timeline for an empty run; does not mutate the model; ascending in-range stops for all four fixtures. frameAt: a fully-formed frame at the start (clamped elapsed, timeMs = startedAt, progress 0, atEnd false, sender AND recipient live); clamps before-start / past-end; linear progress 0->0.5->1; firedCount/cursorIndex monotonic with time and cursorIndex === firedCount-1; activeAgentIds grows across the fan-out (orchestrator+worker_alpha at 0 -> all six at end); a silent recipient-only agent counts as active (dead branch); a zero-span run is one instant (all events fired, progress 1, atEnd); empty run yields cursor -1 / 0 fired / [] / progress 0 / atEnd; deterministic and non-mutating. createPlayhead: paused at 0 on DEFAULT_SPEED 1; clamps an initial position; honours options. Controls: setPlaying/setSpeed identity when unchanged; togglePlay round-trips; cycleSpeed walks the preset ladder both ways with wrapping ([2,4,0.25,0.5,1] up, [0.5,0.25,4,2,1] down); no input mutation. seek: clamps, identity when unchanged, pure. step: forward visits every stop and no-ops at the last (per fixture); backward snaps to the run start before the first stop and steps to the previous stop; steps from an in-between position; preserves speed/playing. advance: no-op when paused or delta<=0; delta scaled by speed (1000ms@1x=1000, @2x=2000); clamps at the span and auto-pauses at the end; keeps playing short of the end; deterministic. Purity guard: the module source (comments stripped) makes no Date.now( / performance.now( / Math.random( call.
M1-T7.verification: npm run lint clean (0 warnings / 0 errors, 24 files, --deny-warnings); npm run typecheck clean; npm run test 127/127 passed (8 files, +36 new); npm run build green (365ms); prettier --check clean repo-wide on the touched files
M1-T7.notes: The pure playback seam of the data layer (PRD §5 names it beside the trace contract/parser/normalization/layout) now exists in src/timeline/ — pure, zero-dep, jsdom-safe, no clock, no randomness, no mutation. buildTimeline(model) flattens a normalized TraceModel into a Timeline: the canonical events (shared, read-only), the distinct event times as `stops` (several events at one instant collapse to one stop and fire together — what makes stepping total over sub-millisecond bursts), agentIds in canonical order, and startedAt/endedAt/spanMs. frameAt(timeline, elapsedMs) is the per-frame query the render layer rides on: it clamps the position into [0, spanMs], binary-searches the last fired event (cursorIndex/firedCount), returns timeMs = startedAt+elapsed, progress, atEnd, and activeAgentIds. DESIGN DECISION: an agent is active if a fired event touches it as SENDER **or RECIPIENT** (a message fires for both ends) or as a tool-call maker — so a silent worker lights up the moment its first assignment lands, not only once it replies; that is the property the spatial scene needs to reveal fan-out/dead-branch over time, and it is why the frame scans message events for `to` rather than only reading event.agentId. activeAgentIds filters the canonical agent list (never the Set's insertion order), so it is stable. The Playhead is a plain immutable value {elapsedMs, speed, playing}; every control is a pure transition returning a new value — createPlayhead, setPlaying, togglePlay, setSpeed, cycleSpeed (walks PLAYBACK_SPEEDS = [0.25,0.5,1,2,4], wrapping, via a direction sign), seek (clamped), stepForward/stepBackward (jump to the next/previous distinct stop; forward no-ops at the last stop, backward snaps to 0 before the first), and advance(playhead, timeline, deltaMs) = elapsed += deltaMs*speed, clamped to the span and AUTO-PAUSING at the end. DETERMINISM IS THE DELIVERABLE (PRD §5): real time is passed IN as deltaMs by the caller's animation loop — the module never reads Date.now/performance.now/Math.random — so the same model+playhead always yields a byte-identical timeline/frame/playhead (pinned by JSON-equality tests), and a purity test scans the module source (comments stripped) to keep it that way. ANTI-DRIFT (PRD §8): this is the SCALAR that drives the spatial scene over time (which arcs have appeared, which nodes are hot, how far the camera has walked) and the substrate for M4-T1's scrubber — it is explicitly NOT a linear replay/search view (AgentReplay/traceview/tracediff cover that); the spatial view remains the product. Deliberately NOT done here: no layout (M2), no rendering/scrubber UI (M3/M4-T1 own the React/Zustand plumbing), no filters (M4-T5). M1 is now complete (all 7 tasks); NEXT per dependency order: M2-T1 (force-directed 3D layout over the agent graph), which depends on the completed M1-T5 + M1-T6.

M2-T1.title: Force-directed 3D layout over the agent graph (seeded, deterministic)

Structure: for all four fixtures connected agents settle nearer than unconnected ones (mean linked < mean unlinked) and the mean link length stays below the mean pairwise distance. Edge cases/options: the empty run yields an empty layout; a lone agent sits at the origin; agents that share no link are still spread apart; zero iterations returns the deterministically-seeded initial placement; a larger idealDistance scales settled links apart; a different seed yields a different shape. M2-T1.verification: npm run lint clean (0 warnings / 0 errors, 27 files, --deny-warnings); npm run typecheck clean; npm run test 155/155 passed (9 files, +28 new); npm run build green (329ms); prettier --write clean on src/layout/forceLayout.ts and --check clean on the other touched files
M2-T1.notes: The M2 spatial layout engine's core now exists: src/layout/ (pure, zero-dep, jsdom-safe — no three.js, no DOM, no clock, no Math.random) exposes layoutTrace(model, options?) and the graph helper deriveLayoutLinks(model). layoutTrace relaxes the agent communication graph into one 3D position per agent with a Fruchterman–Reingold-style simulation: repulsion between every pair (F = k²/d, so nodes never coincide — the force diverges as d→0), attraction along each communication link (F = d²/k · weight, so the more two agents talk the closer they settle), and a per-iteration displacement cap that cools linearly to zero so late iterations only nudge (M2-T2 formalizes the settlement rule on top of exactly this). DETERMINISM IS THE DELIVERABLE (PRD §5): the initial placement is drawn from a seeded mulberry32 PRNG keyed by the run's own contract-level `seed` (never Math.random), and every accumulation iterates in a canonical id-sorted order with a sorted link list, so the same trace yields a byte-identical layout whatever order its arrays arrive in — pinned by tests that reverse every array and still expect byte-equality. The graph it lays out is the raw undirected COMMUNICATION graph read off the messages (both directions of a pair collapse into one weighted link; a broadcast reaches every other agent; a self-message contributes nothing) — an untyped weighted adjacency used purely for positioning; the typed spawn/handoff/message edge MODEL is deliberately left to M2-T4 and is not built here. No coordinates are written back onto the model (the contract stays coordinate-free); the model is not mutated. Degenerate runs are well-formed: an empty run yields an empty layout, a single agent sits at the origin, and agents with no links are still spread apart by repulsion. The result carries the links, the seed, the iteration count, a residual-force `energy` scalar (the convergence signal M2-T2 reads) and min/max/center/radius `bounds` (what M3/M4's camera frames). Deliberately NOT done here: convergence/early-stop criteria and re-layout stability (M2-T2), visual attribute mapping (M2-T3), the typed edge model (M2-T4), the cross-fixture invariant suite (M2-T5), and any rendering (M3) — nothing about the look is asserted (human-held M5-T5). NEXT: M2-T2 (layout settlement rules: stable convergence, no jitter, reproducible re-layout).

M2-T2.title: Layout settlement rules: stable convergence, no jitter, reproducible re-layout
tests_added: src/layout/settlement.test.ts — 21 tests. Stable convergence: a fully-formed Settlement (expectTypeOf) with the documented defaults echoed; all four fixtures converge (converged true, 0 < iterations < cap, finalEnergy <= tolerance, layout.energy === finalEnergy, isSettled true); energyHistory/movementHistory have one entry per iteration and are index-aligned with finalEnergy/finalMovement; the residual force descends from its initial peak and the last 10 energies are all < 1e-3; a looser tolerance stops no later than a tighter one (1e-2 vs 1e-8) and each respects its own threshold; degenerate 0/1-agent runs settle immediately (empty -> [], solo -> origin, iterations 0); a clipped budget runs exactly maxIterations, reports converged false and still returns a well-formed layout. No jitter: every step's movement is <= that step's exponentially-decaying temperature (half*decay^i) and finalMovement <= the last temperature and < 1e-5; the last-100 movement history is monotone (no oscillation); a far larger budget (5000) settles to byte-identical nodes (the shape has stopped moving); settling is idempotent and does not mutate the model. Reproducible re-layout: byte-identical across calls; independent of the order of agents/messages/toolCalls/events; budget-independent nodes across maxIterations 1500/3000/8000; the seed defaults to the model's and an override changes the shape; every agent is placed once in canonical order and connected agents still settle nearer than unconnected ones. isSettled: false for a fixed-budget layoutTrace (energy remains > tolerance) and true for a settled one, with a tolerance override. Purity: the module source makes no Date.now/performance.now/Math.random call, imports no three.js/DOM, and drives the shared forceLayout core (prepareSimulation/relaxIteration/buildLayout) rather than a second force law.
M2-T2.verification: npm run verify green end-to-end — lint 0 warnings / 0 errors (29 files, --deny-warnings); format:check clean; typecheck clean; test 176/176 passed (10 files, +21 new); build green (358ms); prettier --write clean on the 2 reformatted files (forceLayout.ts, settlement.ts)
M2-T2.notes: M2-T2 formalizes the *settlement rule* on top of M2-T1's relaxation, in src/layout/settlement.ts (pure, zero-dep, jsdom-safe — no three.js, no DOM, no clock, no Math.random). settleLayout(model, options?) relaxes until the shape SETTLES and reports exactly how. THE KEY ENGINEERING CALL: M2-T1 cools LINEARLY against the iteration budget (temperature = half·(1−iter/iterations)); measured, that FREEZES rather than equilibrates — the raw residual energy sits at ~10–40 for most of a 2000-iteration run and only collapses in the final few steps (the cap holds the nodes far from balance until it vanishes) — and because the schedule depends on the budget, the same run at a different iteration count is a DIFFERENT shape. So it is a poor settlement rule. The settlement pass instead cools EXPONENTIALLY and INDEPENDENTLY of the budget (temperature(i) = half·decay^i, DEFAULT_DECAY = 0.98). Two things follow: (1) STABLE CONVERGENCE — the residual energy decays geometrically to floating-point zero (a real force balance), so the four fixtures converge in 770–834 iterations at residual <= 1e-6 (DEFAULT_ENERGY_TOLERANCE), well before DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS 2000; (2) REPRODUCIBLE RE-LAYOUT — because the trajectory depends only on the iteration INDEX, the settled configuration is BUDGET-INDEPENDENT: maxIterations 1500, 2000 and 8000 give byte-identical nodes (pinned by a test), which is the strongest available statement of 'stable re-layout'. Honesty: a two-agent graph with no links is reported converged:false with a non-zero final energy (repulsion-only has no finite equilibrium) rather than faked — reported, never invented. TO AVOID A SECOND FORCE LAW, layoutTrace's physics was extracted into a shared core in forceLayout.ts — prepareSimulation (build the seeded initial state), relaxIteration (one step; returns residual energy + the applied max node movement), buildLayout (freeze the state into a ForceLayout) — and layoutTrace was rewritten to drive it. Both primitives now share ONE physics and cannot drift; a source-level guard asserts settlement.ts imports the core. The extraction is byte-for-byte behaviour-preserving: all 28 M2-T1 tests still pass unchanged. The Settlement it returns carries converged, iterations, maxIterations, decay, energyTolerance, energyHistory, movementHistory, finalEnergy and finalMovement; isSettled(layout, tolerance?) reads a layout's residual force. The three named properties are gated as DATA over the fixtures (no visuals — jsdom has no GPU; the look is human-held M5-T5): STABLE CONVERGENCE (converged true, iterations < cap, finalEnergy <= tolerance, energy descends, a looser tolerance stops no later than a tighter one, degenerate 0/1-agent runs settle immediately); NO JITTER (every step is capped by that step's geometrically-decaying temperature, the last-100 movement history is monotone so the shape cannot oscillate, finalMovement < 1e-5, and a much larger budget settles to the identical shape); REPRODUCIBLE RE-LAYOUT (byte-identical across calls, independent of array order, budget-independent nodes, seed default/override). It also re-pins M2-T1's structural property (settlement does not break 'connected agents settle nearer than unconnected'). Pure and deterministic: no clock, no randomness, no model mutation. Deliberately NOT done here: the visual-attribute mapping (M2-T3), the typed spawn/handoff/message edge model (M2-T4), any render/three.js, and NO change to layoutTrace's fixed-budget defaults (M2-T1 stays as-is). NEXT: M2-T3 (visual-attribute mapping: node size/emissive from activity, arc width from message volume).

M2-T3.notes: M2-T3 adds the visual-attribute half of the M2 spatial layout engine, in src/layout/attributes.ts (pure, zero-dep, jsdom-safe — no three.js, no DOM, no clock, no Math.random, no model mutation). mapTraceAttributes(model, options?) turns a normalized TraceModel into the numbers the render layer (M3) draws with: node size + emissive driven by each agent's activity (messagesSent + messagesReceived + toolCalls), and arc width driven by the message volume on each communication link. ARC WIDTH REUSES M2-T1's ADJACENCY: the links come from deriveLayoutLinks, so an arc is drawn exactly along the edge the layout relaxed (undirected, both directions collapsed, a broadcast reaching every other agent) — no second graph is derived (asserted by a source-scan test). NORMALIZATION IS RELATIVE, WITHIN THE RUN: activity is min-max scaled across its agents and volume across its links, each into [0,1] then lerped into the channel's output range (node size 0.25→0.9, emissive 0.15→1, arc radius 0.015→0.12 — calibrated to the layout's unit ideal edge length, tunable, and NOT pinned by a test because the look is human-held). Relative scaling is what gives one run good dynamic range regardless of absolute scale. NO SPREAD => NEUTRAL: when every agent has equal activity or every link equal volume there is no relative signal, so every element gets the midpoint (NEUTRAL_INTENSITY = 0.5) instead of 0/0. Raw activity is exposed on each NodeAttribute (activity: {messagesSent, messagesReceived, toolCalls, total}) and the two normalization spans (activityRange, volumeRange) are returned, so a test or a HUD can read the numbers behind a visual. Tool-call counts are counted from model.toolCalls (the contract has no precomputed per-agent tool-call field); message counts are read from the agent's own precomputed fields. DETERMINISM IS THE DELIVERABLE (PRD §5): the output is a byte-identical function of the trace whatever order its arrays arrive in (agents iterated in canonical id order; links come from the canonical deriveLayoutLinks). Read off the fixtures: fan-out's orchestrator is the hottest node (total 10 = 5 sent + 5 tool calls) against its five silent workers (total 1); the loop's researcher⇄critic chatter (weight 6) is the thickest arc beside the orchestrator's lone kickoff (weight 1); the dead-branch's unanswered worker_dead is the least active node (total 1). Deliberately NOT done here: token/cost visuals (v1 rows carry neither, so every value would be 0), the typed spawn/handoff/message edge model (M2-T4) that refines WHICH arcs exist, colour/hue selection, and the bloom calibration (M3-T4). M2-T4.title: Derived edge model: spawn/handoff/message edges from the trace, never hand-placed
M2-T4.tests_added: src/layout/edges.test.ts — 36 tests. Shape: a fully-formed EdgeModel (expectTypeOf); EDGE_KINDS pinned to exactly ['spawn','handoff','message']; one lineage per agent in canonical id order; byKind groups equal the kind-filtered edges and counts agree; the edge list is ordered canonically (kind-rank, then source, then target). Classification: classifyAction reads a coordination verb (assign_task, start_loop, spawn_agent, delegate_work, dispatch, kickoff) as spawn, a relay verb (handoff / hand_off / hand-off / relay_task / escalate / transfer) as handoff, splits camelCase (assignTask -> spawn), checks handoff before spawn (relay_assign), and treats anything else — a draft, a revise, task_complete, assignment_complete, review_complete, '' or null — as an ordinary message (only the leading verb classifies). Per-fixture structure: fan-out is five orchestrator->worker spawn edges of weight 1 (actions ['assign_task']) with the orchestrator a coordinator and parent of all five (maxFanOut 5, rootIds [a_orchestrator]); loop is a kickoff spawn orchestrator->researcher beside two directed message edges (researcher<->critic, weight 3 each, actions draft / revise) and the never-spawned critic still reads worker; dead-branch is two orchestrator spawns plus a worker_ok->orchestrator task_complete message (maxFanOut 2); handoff-chain is the three-edge relay a->b->c->d with no spawn, every agent a root, the initiator a coordinator and the rest workers. Direction/targets: a two-way exchange stays TWO edges (not the collapsed layout link); a broadcast reaches every other agent and never its sender; a self-message contributes no edge; an inline action-bearing message classifies into spawn/handoff/message. Lineage: an agent that only ever receives is a participant (worker), not an invented 'external'; a spawn fan-in keeps both edges but picks the earliest spawner as parent; a spawn cycle throws DerivedEdgeError; an empty run is well-formed; an agent with no edges is 'unknown'. Lookups: lineageOf finds / returns null; edgeBetween is direction- and kind-specific. withDerivedLineage fills role/parentId, is a fixed point of normalizeTrace, accepts a pre-derived model, and does not mutate. Determinism: byte-identical across calls; independent of the array order; non-mutating. Purity: the module source reads no clock / Math.random, imports no three.js/DOM, and derives a distinct graph from the layout adjacency (no forceLayout import).

M2-T4.notes: M2-T4 adds the typed edge model to src/layout/edges.ts (pure, zero-dep, jsdom-safe — no three.js, no DOM, no clock, no Math.random, no model mutation). deriveEdgeModel(model) turns the trace's messages into typed, DIRECTED relationships and, from the spawn edges, derives the two Agent fields M1-T5 deliberately deferred to this pass: role and parentId. THE THREE KINDS (the product's structural questions): spawn (a coordination act that puts another agent to work), handoff (the baton passing on), message (everything else). CLASSIFICATION IS DERIVED, NEVER HAND-PLACED: each message is classified from its declared action by matching the action's FIRST word (camelCase split, non-alphanumerics stripped) against verb tables — handoff checked before spawn; unmatched or action-less messages are plain 'message' edges, so the model never invents a stronger relationship than the trace states (assignment_complete is a message; assign_task is a spawn). DIRECTION IS PRESERVED: unlike deriveLayoutLinks (M2-T1, which collapses a pair into ONE undirected weighted link for the shape), this model keeps researcher->critic and critic->researcher as two edges — the relationship is directional (a spawn points at its child, a handoff at its successor). A broadcast yields one message edge to every other agent; a self-message contributes nothing. Edges aggregate by (kind, source, target) with weight/messageIds/actions/firstAt/lastAt and are sorted canonically (kind-rank, then source, then target). LINEAGE: parentId is the earliest spawner (deterministic tie-break by parent id when several agents spawn the same child — both spawn edges are kept, so fan-in stays visible); role is coordinator (spawns children, even if itself spawned — a sub-orchestrator), worker (was spawned, or otherwise participates), coordinator for the run's initiator, and unknown for an agent touched by nothing. ENGINEERING CALL: the first draft assigned an 'external' role to any agent that only ever received, but that mislabels a dead-branch terminal leaf and the end of a handoff chain as external — v1's agent_messages graph carries no signal that separates an external endpoint from a dead leaf, nor a human from an agent, so those two roles are NEVER invented here (documented; a plain sink reads worker). FAIL LOUDLY: a spawn cycle (an agent that is its own ancestor) throws DerivedEdgeError rather than being silently repaired — the same rule normalization uses. DETERMINISM IS THE DELIVERABLE (PRD §5): it iterates the model in canonical order and sorts its output, so the same trace yields a byte-identical EdgeModel whatever order the arrays arrive in (pinned by a test that reverses every array), and the model is never mutated. withDerivedLineage(model) writes the derived roles/parents back onto the contract and is a fixed point of normalizeTrace (M1-T5 preserves role/parentId), so a consumer can hand the render layer an enriched model. Deliberately NOT done here: re-deriving the layout adjacency (M2-T1 owns it), changing the visual mapping (M2-T3 shipped; wiring arcs to edge kinds is a later refinement), and the cross-fixture invariant sweep (M2-T5). NEXT: M2-T5 (layout + attribute invariant tests across all fixtures).

M2-T5.notes: M2-T5 adds the shared cross-fixture invariant gate that ties M2-T1..T4 together, in src/layout/invariants.ts (pure, zero-dep, jsdom-safe — no three.js, no DOM, no clock, no Math.random, no mutation of any input). M2-T1..T4 each tested themselves in isolation; this module expresses the M2 exit criteria once, as data, and runs them over ALL FOUR fixtures — the point of the task ('an invariant proven on one fixture is proven on all of them') and the thing M3's draw-call gate (M3-T5) and M5's scale proof (M5-T1) will reuse. It returns InvariantViolation[] (empty ⇒ holds) rather than throwing, so a caller decides what to do with a report; assertInvariants is the throwing convenience and InvariantError carries the violations plus a message naming each code. THREE CHECKS + a rollup. (1) checkLayoutInvariants — one node per agent in canonical id order (count/order/uniqueness via a shared checkIndexById helper); finite, distinct positions (>= MIN_DISTANCE apart — repulsion’s job); the layout is pinned to the run’s seed and reports a non-negative integer iteration count (and 0 for a 0/1-agent run); energy finite and >= 0; bounds enclose every node, center is the min/max midpoint and radius is the farthest node (within 1e-9); and the link list IS deriveLayoutLinks(model) deep-equal — the topology derives from the trace, it is never authored — plus link validity/sort/uniqueness. (2) checkAttributeInvariants — one node per agent; every activity figure re-derives from the model's own agent counts and tool-call list; total sums its parts; intensity in [0,1]; size/emissive/width within the configured output range; more activity never reads dimmer (monotone); the recorded activityRange/volumeRange are the TRUE spans; arcs mirror the layout’s links; and a channel with no spread is neutral (NEUTRAL_INTENSITY). (3) checkEdgeInvariants — edges partition into byKind with agreeing counts; canonical order (kind rank, then source, then target); each edge re-derives from the messages it aggregates (weight === messageIds.length, ids resolve, direction matches — including a broadcast’s to===null, classification matches classifyAction, firstAt/lastAt are the min/max, actions are the distinct sorted set); and the spawn lineage is a coherent forest — real acyclic parents, childIds/fanOut/maxFanOut/rootIds consistent, and every role re-derived from the documented rule (the checker re-implements the rule and compares, so a drifted role fails). checkSceneInvariants(model, options) is the end-to-end rollup: settle + map + derive, then all three checks — the M2 exit criteria in one call. It deliberately RE-DERIVES every expected value from the model rather than trusting the layer’s own internals, so a drifted implementation fails loudly instead of self-agreeing. The second machine-gate half is findHandAuthoredCoordinates(source): a pure scanner that flags a new Vector3(…) / a position: [...] or position: {x:…} literal / a NON-ZERO {x,y,z} triple (a symbolically-zero origin is a sentinel, so it is allowed), comments stripped — a test walks the ten pure data-layer modules (types/adapter/model/fixtures/timeline/layout) and asserts none carries a hand-placed coordinate (the render layer’s camera config, e.g. Viewport.tsx’s position: [0,0,12], is explicitly out of scope — it is a camera, not an agent). THE TESTS ALSO PROVE THE HARNESS IS NOT VACUOUS: each check is fed a deliberately broken layout / attribute map / edge model and asserts it names the right code. DETERMINISM: the full M2 derivation (settle + attributes + edges) is byte-identical across two runs and independent of array order, on every fixture. NO visuals asserted — jsdom has no GPU; the look is human-held (M5-T5). Deliberately NOT done here: no new rendering, no per-fixture shape assertions (M2-T1..T4 already pin those). The plan composes the two M2 passes — settleLayout (M2-T1+M2-T2, the deterministic seeded shape) and mapTraceAttributes (M2-T3, activity -> size/emissive) — joined by agentId into one NodeInstance per agent: settled position, radius (= attribute size), intensity, emissive, per-instance glow colour (base RGB x emissive) and — the piece the render layer must not own — the finished column-major 4x4 instance matrix (translation x uniform scale), so the component only copies numbers into the GPU. M3-T2.title: Message arcs as batched animated GLSL curves (not one mesh per message)
tests_added: src/scene/arcs.test.ts — 63 tests over the PURE arc plan and the geometry/shader contract. Structure: one arc per communication link in canonical order on all four fixtures; exactly 1 draw call for the whole arc population; volume/intensity/width read straight from M2-T3's LinkAttribute; the layout/attributes it composed are byte-identical to settleLayout/mapTraceAttributes with seed/bounds/converged/iterations carried through; every arc starts at its source's settled position and ends at its target's; expectTypeOf over the plan, buffers, style and animation shapes. Batched buffers: every attribute is vertexCount x its declared size (ARC_ATTRIBUTE_SIZES); the attribute set is exactly ARC_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTES plus position/normal; each arc owns a contiguous non-overlapping vertex/index slice and the slices tile the batch ((segments+1) x sides vertices, segments x sides x 6 indices); every index names a real vertex and no vertex is orphaned; each arc's own aPhase/aSpeed/aFlow/aIntensity is written onto every one of its vertices and aT runs 0 -> 1. Geometry: every vertex is exactly one tube radius off its arc's quadratic Bezier and the ring's radial offsets cancel onto the curve point; every ring normal is unit and perpendicular to the curve tangent (a transported frame, so the tube cannot twist); every triangle is wound outward (the cross product agrees with the vertex normals); the whole batch stays within the settled cloud's bounds plus its own bow; the control point is the chord midpoint pushed off the chord by bulge x chord with the apex half that far out and both endpoints untouched; bulge 0 gives a straight tube along the chord; perpendicularOf is unit, perpendicular, deterministic and never degenerate (axis-aligned, diagonal, skewed and zero-length axes). Traffic direction: forward+backward equals the link's own weight on every fixture (the arc aggregates exactly the messages the layout weighed); fan-out's five silent workers read as outward traffic; the loop's balanced researcher<->critic channel parks while its kickoff travels at the min rate; dead-branch parks the answered channel and travels the unanswered one; the handoff relay travels a->b->c->d; a reverse-dominant pair reads -1; a broadcast counts once per recipient (the layout's own weight rule) and a self-message counts for nothing. Animation: the rate lerps with volume from the min to the max; a balanced channel gets speed 0 and PARKED_PULSE_PHASE and never moves; the per-pair phase is stable, inside [0,1) and unsynchronised across a fan-out; the pulse parameter stays inside [0,1) for negative, pre-zero and huge times; it repeats with the channel's own period; forward advances 0.1 of a cycle where reverse retreats the same and the two are mirror images; a zero-speed channel holds its phase. Shader contract: the GLSL declares exactly the geometry's custom attributes (never re-declaring position/normal/uv) and exactly the uniforms buildArcUniforms provides, per stage; every varying is written by the vertex stage and read by the fragment stage; the vertex shader keeps the pure rule's shape (uTime * aSpeed + aPhase, fract, aFlow < 0.0) so the GPU twin cannot silently diverge; the fragment stage measures the band in arc parameter with wrap-around. Uniforms: uTime starts at 0 (the render layer owns the tick); the material constants default deterministically, honour overrides and sanitize a bad one; each call returns fresh slots. Style/options: defaults pinned; overrides resize the batch and floor a degenerate resolution (segments >= 1, sides >= 3, pulse width > 0); a swapped pulse-rate pair is tolerated; a bad colour is sanitized per component; a supplied layout/attributeMap is reused by identity (no re-settle), the arcs then meet exactly the node layer's instances and the reused and re-settled plans are byte-identical; settlement overrides pass through; ScenePlanError is named. Determinism/purity: byte-identical across calls; byte-identical under scrambled input arrays; the model is never mutated; endpoints and buffers are owned, so a mutated layout cannot corrupt a built plan; a channel with no volume spread sits at the neutral rate. Purity guard reads src/scene/arcs.ts and src/scene/arcShader.ts off disk: no clock, no randomness, no three/@react-three/DOM, the plan composes settleLayout + mapTraceAttributes + isSettled (not a second implementation), the GLSL is generated from ARC_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTES/ARC_UNIFORMS, and findHandAuthoredCoordinates() finds nothing.

M3-T2.notes: M3-T2 lands the message-arc layer in the PRD §5 split: a PURE plan (src/scene/arcs.ts) + a PURE shader module (src/scene/arcShader.ts) + a THIN mesh (src/scene/MessageArcLayer.tsx). buildArcScenePlan(model, options?) sweeps ONE TUBE PER COMMUNICATION LINK into a SINGLE batched geometry: the curve is a quadratic Bezier from the source's settled position to the target's, bowed off the chord along perpendicularOf(chord) — the world axis the chord is least aligned with, crossed with it, so the bow axis is deterministic and never near-degenerate — and the tube ((segments+1) x sides vertices, triangle index buffer wound CCW about the outward radial) is swept with a PARALLEL-TRANSPORTED frame so it cannot twist. The radius is the link's own `width` from M2-T3, and endpoint positions are COPIED, not referenced, so a reused layout can never mutate a built plan. PRD GEOMETRY BUDGET HONOURED: the batch unit is the LINK, not the message — deriveLayoutLinks already collapsed every message between a pair into one weighted channel — so the whole population lands in one geometry drawn in ONE call (ARC_LAYER_DRAW_CALLS, reported as plan.drawCalls for M3-T5 to aggregate); no per-message mesh and no per-link mesh either; an empty layer costs 0 draw calls. THE ANIMATION IS DERIVED, NOT DECORATIVE: each arc carries a pulse RATE lerped from its normalized volume (M2-T3's own intensity) and a travel DIRECTION taken from the channel's NET traffic — forward and backward message counts, canonically oriented, computed with the same broadcast rule deriveLayoutLinks uses, so forward+backward === the link's weight exactly (pinned by tests). A BALANCED channel (equal traffic both ways) gets speed 0 and PARKED_PULSE_PHASE and simply does not travel: the trace shows no net direction there, and inventing one would be the same class of error as hand-placing a coordinate. (Flagged for the human look review — M5-T5 may prefer a different read of a balanced channel.) The per-pair phase is an FNV-1a hash of the pair, so arcs are not synchronised and nothing is random. The fixtures therefore read their own structure: the fan-out's five links all pulse outward, the loop's hot researcher<->critic channel is parked while its kickoff travels, the dead branch's unanswered assignment travels while the answered one parks, and the handoff relay travels a->b->c->d. THE SHADER IS GENERATED FROM THE PLAN'S CONTRACT: arcShader.ts builds its `attribute float ...;` lines from ARC_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTES — the list the geometry writes — and its `uniform <type> <name>;` lines from ARC_UNIFORMS, the list buildArcUniforms fills, so a geometry attribute the shader forgot (or a shader attribute the geometry never provides) is structurally impossible; a test pins that two-way equality per stage, plus the varyings and the pulse formula. The GPU twin of the pure rule arcPulseParameter is `fract(uTime * aSpeed + aPhase)` flipped by `aFlow < 0.0`; the pure function is the reference implementation and a test asserts the GLSL keeps that shape — the same canary M3-T1 applies to three.js Matrix4.compose. THE CLOCK STAYS IN THE RENDER LAYER: uTime starts at 0 and MessageArcLayer advances it in useFrame (state.clock.elapsedTime); the pure layer takes time as a PARAMETER, so the rule is unit-testable in jsdom while the tick lives where the PRD puts it. Buffers are plain number[] (JSON-serialisable, deterministic) so the plan stays pure and three converts them to typed attributes on upload; the component builds ONE BufferGeometry, disposes it when the plan changes or it unmounts, and draws additively with depthWrite off, so nodes occlude arcs and arcs do not occlude each other. Viewport mounts the arc layer beside the node layer for the same run; both settle the layout independently and deterministically so they agree exactly, and M3-T6 is where the two derivations consolidate into one shared scene pass (which is also where the double settle should go before M5's scale work). NOT gated: the look (jsdom has no GPU; human-held M5-T5). The one artifact jsdom cannot exercise was instead verified out of band: the resolved shader text compiles under glslangValidator 16.6.0 for GLSL ES 1.00 and desktop GLSL 1.10 with a three.js-equivalent prefix, and the compiler rejects broken shaders, so the clean result means something. Deliberately NOT done here: the tool-call glyphs (M3-T3); the lighting/bloom emissive calibration (M3-T4) — the two colours and the glow constants are documented placeholders, not a calibration; colouring arcs by the M2-T4 edge KIND (that model refines relationships, not which channels exist); and the M3-T6 fixture mount.
